steps.narration: Most phone finders hand you whatever number shows up first on a search page: an office in another country, a fax line, sometimes a number that doesn't exist. LinkFinder AI looks up the real value for the company you name. Here's exactly how, one click at a time.
Now the company website. Pick company website.
Same company, Yellowstone Landscape. Enrich.
There it is: yellowstonelandscape dot com.
Now the LinkedIn company page. Click Change. Pick LinkedIn company page.

steps.narration: Same company, Yellowstone Landscape. Enrich.
There it is: info at yellowstonelandscape dot com.
Step one. Click Change, then click Phone number.
Step two. Pick Company name, main line. It costs one credit.
Step three. Type the company name: Yellowstone Landscape.
Step four. Click Enrich Data.
There it is: 877, 785, 6685. The real one, not a guess.
Checking companies one at a time is fine for one pitch. For a whole list, click Change, pick the same lookup, and switch to Upload CSV.
Select your file. One column of company names. Ours has 6.
You see every row before anything runs, so you know exactly what it costs.
Click Process 6 items.
Every row gets the exact same lookup. The phone numbers fill in one by one.
6 companies in, 6 phone numbers out, each marked Found. Export it as a CSV in one click.
Your list already lives in Google Sheets? The add-on runs the same lookups right in the column, no export, no re-import.
Want it in your own tools? Click API and MCP in the top menu. Same lookup, one call, the answer comes straight back.
And every lookup lands in History, so you can see what you found, when, and what it cost.
